page.layout: One page of running text on the left printed page (p. 172), with the catchword "&" at the foot right. The right strip of the scan is the edge of the facing page and is not transcribed.

main_text.p: Quia verò Deus vulgò per me-dia eligit, vocat & mittit operarios in messem suam, similiter docetur in scriptura s, quorum voce & suffragiis illa electio & vocario fieri debeat. Ita act 6.6. dicitur, diaconos esse electos & vocatos, convocatâ ab apostolis ecclesiâ; act.14.13. Paulus & Barnabas dicuntur constituisse presbyteros in singulis ecclesiis, non quòd sibi solis illius auctoritatem arrogaverint, sed χειροτονήσαντες [?]; quæ vox 2.Cor.8.19. usurpatur de electione, quæ fit ecclesiæ totius voce seu suffragiis, quæ porrectis manibus, ex consuetudine Græcorum, fieri solebant. Similiter 1.Tim.4. 14. legitur, quòd non tantùm apostoli; sed etiam presbyterorum cætus Timotheo manus imposuerit.

page.notes: The first paragraph's indent marks a new paragraph, so it does not continue from the previous page. The Greek word χειροτονήσαντες is read from a small, faint print and is marked [?]. The long s in "scriptura s," is rendered as a plain s. The "&" at the foot is a catchword pointing to the next page ("& apostoli" at the top of the facing page). The show-through mark at lower left and the binding clip on the left edge are not transcribed.
